36	
37	## Add a text clip
38	
39	Press <kbd>T</kbd>, or click **Add Text** in the timeline bar, the **Aa** button. There's no menu item for it.
40	
41	The new clip reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, in white, centred on the canvas, and it lasts 5 seconds. For a look sized to your canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).
42	
43	It lands at the playhead on the front-most track if it fits there, and on a new track in front of everything if it doesn't. Either way it's one undo step, **Add Text**. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the front-most track is the nest's own.
44	
45	The clip comes in selected, so the canvas shows its handles and the **Clip** tab opens on its **Text** sub-tab. If the inspector is showing **Transcript** or **Assistant**, it stays there.
46	
47	## Change the length
48	
49	Five seconds is only where a text clip starts. With no source file to run out of, you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length.
50	
51	## Write the words
52	
53	There are two places to type:
54	
55	- **On the canvas.** Double-click the clip in the preview. See [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
56	- **In the inspector.** Select the clip and use the **Content** section at the top of the **Text** sub-tab. It's the one Text section that starts open. Its header shows the first line of the text, or "empty".
57	
58	In the **Content** box:
59	
60	| Key | What it does |
61	| --- | --- |
62	| <kbd>Return</kbd> | Applies the text, and the single-letter shortcuts work again |
63	| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Applies the text the same way, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings |
64	| <kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd> or <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> | Starts a new line |
65	
66	A click elsewhere in the window, below its title bar, applies the text too. Changing the words is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If they haven't changed, there's no undo step.
67	
68	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Content** sets the words at that action's end. Words don't ease from one to another, so the text switches when the action ends.
69	
70	## Style the clip
71	
72	The **Text** sub-tab has the rest of a clip's look, and each section has its own page:
73	
74	| Section | Page |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| **Font** and **Style** | [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) |
77	| **Outline** and **Backdrop** | [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) |
78	| **Box** | [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) |
79	| **Reveal** | [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) |
80	| **Presets** | [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/) |
81	
82	The sub-tab shows only when every selected clip is a text clip. With several selected, a change goes to all of them.
83	
84	## Place it and add effects
85	
86	A text clip also has a **Picture** sub-tab, with these sections in this order:
87	
88	- [Transform](/canvas/transform/), for position, scale, rotation and opacity
89	- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), which isn't shown while a nest is open
90	- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
91	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
92	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
93	- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
94	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
95	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)
96	
97	Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, because they work on a clip's source pixels. A text clip has no **Color** or **Sound** sub-tab.
98	
99	## With an agent
100	
101	`add_text_clip` needs a track and a time. It can also set the length, 5 seconds if left out, and the words and the whole look in the same call. Unlike <kbd>T</kbd>, it doesn't fall back to a new track: if the clip would overlap another, Frame Job won't add it.
102	
103	`set_text` changes any mix of a clip's words and typography in one undo step. An agent isn't held to the ranges of the inspector's fields, so a size above 800 px is fine, for example. Position and scale go through `set_video`. Word timings sent for a caption must match its number of words, or the call fails and gives both numbers. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_text_clip) and [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
104	
105	## Good to know
106	
107	A caption is a text clip too. If one is timed word by word, editing it keeps the timings while the number of words stays the same. Change the number of words and it loses its timing, so its words no longer change as they're spoken, and **Content** notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/) and [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
108

116	---
117	title: Font and text style
118	description: Choose a text clip's font and size, then set its colour, alignment, capitals, line spacing and letter spacing.
119	---
120	
121	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
122	
123	The **Font** and **Style** sections of the **Text** sub-tab set how a text clip's words look. Select a text clip to reach them. Both start closed, so click a header to open its section. The **Font** header shows the size and the **Style** header shows the alignment.
124	
125	<AtAGlance
126	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Style']}
127	  tools="set_text"
128	/>
129	
130	## Choose a font
131	
132	**Family** lists every font family installed on your Mac, plus the ones Frame Job ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono.
133	
134	**Style** lists the faces of that family, such as Regular or SemiBold.
135	
136	When you change **Family**, Frame Job keeps the current style if the new family has one of that name. Otherwise it uses Regular, or the family's first style if it has no Regular. Both controls make an undo step called **Font**.
137	
138	See [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) for more on the faces.
139	
140	## Set the size
141	
142	**Size** runs from 6 to 800 px, and a new clip starts at 72 px. Type a value or use the quick picks: 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144.
143	
144	The size is in canvas pixels, so the same number looks smaller on a larger canvas. For a size worked out from the canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).
145	
146	## Set the colour
147	
148	**Color** is white by default. Click its swatch to open the colour panel, and set the colour and its opacity there.
149	
150	## Align the text
151	
152	| Control | Choices | Default |
153	| --- | --- | --- |
154	| **Align** | **L**, **C** or **R** | Centre |
155	| **Vertical** | Top, middle or bottom of the box | Middle |
156	
157	Both make an undo step called **Alignment**.
158	
159	With the box on **Auto-size**, the box is as wide as the longest line, so **Align** lines up the shorter lines and a single line doesn't move. In a [fixed-width box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/), it places every line in the box. To move the text itself, drag it on the canvas or use [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
160	
161	A text box is always as tall as its words, so **Vertical** moves the text by a pixel or two at most.
162	
163	## Show the text in capitals
164	
165	Tick **UPPERCASE** to draw the text in capitals. What you typed is kept as you typed it, so unticking the box brings it back. It never changes the number of words, so it's safe on captions timed word by word.
166	
167	The [canvas text editor](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) shows the text as you typed it, not in capitals.
168	
169	## Adjust the spacing
170	
171	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
172	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
173	| **Line spacing** | The space between lines, as a multiple of the font's line height | 1× | 0.5 to 4× |
174	| **Tracking** | Extra space between letters. Below 0 pulls them together. | 0 px | −20 to 100 px |
175	
176	## Reset the style
177	
178	**Reset** in the **Style** section's header puts everything in that section back, in one undo step called **Text Style**:
179	
180	- **Color** to white
181	- **Align** to centre and **Vertical** to middle
182	- **UPPERCASE** off
183	- **Line spacing** to 1× and **Tracking** to 0 px
184	
185	It shows while something in the section differs from those values and no action is selected. It doesn't touch the font or the size, and the **Font** section has no **Reset** of its own. To put **Size** back to 72 px, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
186	
187	## Change the style during a clip
188	
189	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Size**, **Color**, **Line spacing** and **Tracking** ease towards the new value, and colours [blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab). **Family**, **Style**, **Align**, **Vertical** and **UPPERCASE** switch when the action ends.
190	
191	## With an agent
192	
193	An agent names a font by its one PostScript name, such as `SourceSans3-Bold`, rather than by family and style. A colour is four numbers from 0 to 1: red, green, blue and opacity. **Align** is `align` (`left`, `center` or `right`), **Vertical** is `valign` (`top`, `middle` or `bottom`), and **UPPERCASE** is `case` (`as_written` or `upper`).
194	
195	An agent isn't held to the ranges above: a size or line spacing only has to be above 0, and tracking can be any number. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
196	
197	## Good to know
198	
199	A project can name a font this Mac doesn't have. The **Text** sub-tab still opens, showing the first family in the list, and the text draws in a substitute until you install the font or choose another.
200

208	---
209	title: Edit text on the canvas
210	description: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type into it, then apply, add new lines or back out.
211	---
212	
213	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
214	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
215	
216	You can type straight into a text clip in the preview, and see the words wrap where they'll sit in the picture.
217	
218	<AtAGlance
219	  keys={['Return', '⇧Return', 'Esc']}
220	  where="Double-click a text clip in the preview"
221	  tools="set_text"
222	/>
223	
224	## Type on the canvas
225	
226	<Steps>
227	
228	1. Move the playhead so the clip is on the canvas.
229	
230	2. Double-click the clip. The editor opens over it with all the text selected.
231	
232	3. Type. The editor grows and wraps as you go, the way the text will once applied.
233	
234	4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> to apply.
235	
236	</Steps>
237	
238	The editor uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, so the lines break where they will in the picture. It draws in the interface's own colours, not the clip's, so you can always read what you're typing.
239	
240	**UPPERCASE** text shows as you typed it. A rotated clip's editor stays upright, and the text you apply is the same either way.
241	
242	Opening the editor leaves [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). Double-clicking any other kind of clip enters it.
243	
244	## Apply the text
245	
246	Any of these applies the text and closes the editor:
247	
248	- <kbd>Return</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd>
249	- <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings
250	- A click elsewhere in the window, below its title bar
251	
252	Applying is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If the words haven't changed, there's no undo step. After <kbd>Return</kbd> the keys go back to the canvas, so its single-letter keys work again.
253	
254	## Start a new line
255	
256	<kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd> and <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> all start a new line. Caps Lock and <kbd>fn</kbd> don't count, so <kbd>Return</kbd> with either of those still applies.
257	
258	## Leave with Esc
259	
260	Over unchanged text, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the editor at once.
261	
262	Over changed text, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?", and reminds you that "Return applies while you type; ⇧Return starts a new line."
263	
264	| Button | What it does |
265	| --- | --- |
266	| **Apply** | Keeps your text and closes the editor. It's the default, on <kbd>Return</kbd>. |
267	| **Revert** | Closes the editor and drops your changes. |
268	| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing. <kbd>Esc</kbd> in the sheet does the same. |
269	
270	While the sheet is up, clicking away doesn't apply the text behind your back.
271	
272	## Use an input method
273	
274	While an input method is composing, <kbd>Return</kbd>, keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Esc</kbd> go to the input method, not the editor. They do their usual jobs again once the composition ends.
275	
276	## Good to know
277	
278	- You can only double-click what's on the canvas, and a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) can't be picked there. To change those words, use **Content** in the [Text sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#write-the-words).
279	- The editor always changes the clip's own words, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To change the words at an action's end, use **Content**.
280	- On a caption timed word by word, changing the number of words drops the page's timing. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#good-to-know).

298	<AtAGlance
299	  where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets"
300	  tools={['set_text', 'set_video']}
301	/>
302	
303	## Apply a preset
304	
305	<Steps>
306	
307	1. Select one or more text clips.
308	
309	2. Open the **Presets** section at the bottom of the **Text** sub-tab. It starts closed.
310	
311	3. Click **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Lower Third** or **Caption**.
312	
313	</Steps>
314	
315	It's one undo step, named after the preset.
316	
317	## The four presets
318	
319	| Preset | Font | Size | At 1920 × 1080 | Align | Position | Backdrop |
320	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
321	| **Title** | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | 97 px | Centre | Centre of the canvas | None |
322	| **Subtitle** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | 54 px | Centre | 18 % of the height below centre | None |
323	| **Lower Third** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | 49 px | Left | 20 % of the width left of centre, 28 % of the height below it | Black at 55 %, padding 18 px, radius 6 px |
324	| **Caption** | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | 38 px | Centre | 38 % of the height below centre | Black at 60 %, padding 12 px, radius 8 px |
325	
326	The position is where the centre of the text's box sits, so a longer name on a **Lower Third** grows both ways from that point.
327	
328	**Title** isn't the look a new text clip starts with. That has the same font at a fixed 72 px, where **Title** works its size out from the canvas.
329	
330	On a canvas taller than wide, **Caption** sits higher, a quarter of the height below centre, clear of a phone's on-screen controls.
331	
332	[Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) from **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and **File ▸ Import Captions…** use the **Caption** look, and they also wrap at 80 % of the canvas width. The **Caption** button itself leaves the [box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) as it is.
333	
334	## How a preset fits the canvas
335	
336	Sizes are a share of the canvas's shorter side, and positions a share of its width and height. So a preset fits any canvas, and a vertical 1080 × 1920 canvas gets the same text height as a 1920 × 1080 one. A backdrop's padding and radius stay at the pixel values in the table.
337	
338	The size is worked out once, from the canvas at the moment you click. Changing the canvas afterwards doesn't apply the preset again.
339	
340	## What a preset changes
341	
342	As well as the settings in the table, a preset sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %. **Title** and **Subtitle** take away any backdrop.
343	
344	It leaves everything else alone, including the words, the colour, the outline, tracking, line spacing, **UPPERCASE**, the box, the reveal, scale and rotation.
345	
346	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a preset sets that action's end, like any other field.
347	
348	## With an agent
349	
350	There's no preset tool. An agent sends the same values through `set_text` and `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
351	
352	## Related
353	
354	- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
355	- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
356	- [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/)
357	=== text-outline-and-backdrop
358	---
359	title: Text outline and backdrop
360	description: Draw a stroke around a text clip's letters, or put a rounded plate behind them, so the words stay readable over any picture.
361	---
362	
363	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
364	
365	White words get lost over a bright shot. An outline draws a stroke around each letter, and a backdrop puts a rounded plate behind the whole text. You can use either or both.
366	
367	<AtAGlance
368	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Outline', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Backdrop']}
369	  tools="set_text"
370	/>
371	
372	## Add an outline
373	
374	Select a text clip, click the **Outline** header in the **Text** sub-tab to open the section, and tick **Outline**. You get a 2 px black stroke.
375	
376	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
377	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
378	| **Width** | The stroke's thickness. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 2 px | 0 to 40 px |
379	| **Color** | The stroke's colour | Black | |
380	
381	Both are greyed while the outline is off. The section's header shows the width, or "off".
382	
383	The stroke sits on the edge of each letter, half inside and half outside, so a wide outline thins the letters.
384	
385	**Reset** in the section's header turns the outline off.
386	
387	## Add a backdrop
388	
389	Click the **Backdrop** header to open the section, and tick **Backdrop**. You get a black plate at 60 % opacity.
390	
391	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
392	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
393	| **Fill** | The plate's colour and opacity | Black at 60 % | |
394	| **Padding** | The space between the text and the plate's edge. Quick picks: 0, 8, 12, 24 and 48. | 12 px | 0 to 200 px |
395	| **Radius** | How round the corners are. Quick picks: 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32. | 8 px | 0 to 200 px |
396	
397	All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. The section's header shows the padding, or "off".
398	
399	A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.
400	
401	**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.
402	
403	## Change them during a clip
404	
405	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours [blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab). Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.
406	
407	## With an agent
408	
409	`set_text` sets both. `outline` takes `width` and `color`, and `backdrop` takes `color`, `padding` and `radius`. Send `null` for either to turn it off. An agent isn't held to the ranges above: a width, padding or radius only has to be 0 or more. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
410	
411	## Good to know
412	
413	- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
414	- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
415	- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.
416	
417	## Related
418	
419	- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
420	- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
421	- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
422	=== text-box
423	---
424	title: "Text box and wrapping"
425	description: "Let a text clip's box fit its words, or set a width and have the words wrap, from the inspector or by dragging on the canvas."
426	---
427	
428	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
429	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
430	
431	A text clip's box decides where its lines break. By default the box fits the words, and only your own line breaks start a new line. Give it a fixed width and the words wrap to fit.
432	
433	<AtAGlance
434	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Box', 'Drag a text clip\'s left or right handle on the canvas']}
435	  tools="set_text"
436	/>
437	
438	## Wrap text at a width
439	
440	<Steps>
441	
442	1. Select the text clip.
443	
444	2. In the inspector's **Clip** tab, open the **Box** section of the **Text** sub-tab.
445	
446	3. Set **Mode** to **Fixed width**. The width starts at 60 % of the canvas width, which is 1,152 px on a 1920-wide canvas.
447	
448	4. Type a **Width**, or drag a [side handle](#drag-the-width-on-the-canvas) on the canvas.
449	
450	</Steps>
451	
452	To go back, set **Mode** to **Auto-size** or choose the section's **Reset**.
453	
454	## The Box section
455	
456	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
457	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
458	| **Mode** | **Auto-size** lays the text out without wrapping, so the box fits the words. **Fixed width** wraps the words at **Width**. | Auto-size | |
459	| **Width** | The width the words wrap at. It's greyed in Auto-size. | 60 % of the canvas width | 20 to 20,000 px |
460	
461	A number typed outside the range is brought back to the nearest limit. When the section is closed, its header reads "auto", or the width, such as "1152 px".
462	
463	## Drag the width on the canvas
464	
465	Drag a text clip's left or right handle in the preview to set its wrap width. If the box was on Auto-size, it becomes **Fixed width**, starting from the box's current width.
466	
467	The text stays centred on the same point and grows both ways, whichever handle you drag. The drag holds the width between 4 and 20,000 px, so it can go narrower than the 20 px the **Width** field lets you type.
468	
469	The other handles do something different. The corners and the top and bottom handles scale the text uniformly and leave the wrap width alone. See [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).
470	
471	## What a fixed width changes
472	
473	- **The height follows the lines.** A fixed width sets only the width, and the box grows taller as the text wraps onto more lines.
474	- **Alignment works across the whole width.** Left, centre and right [alignment](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) line the words up against the width you set, not against the longest line.
475	- **A backdrop fills the whole box.** A [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) is as wide as **Width** plus its padding on each side, even when the words are shorter. **Width** measures the words, and the padding sits outside it.
476	
477	## Good to know
478	
479	- In Auto-size a long line never wraps, so it can run off the canvas. Press <kbd>⇧Return</kbd> in the [text area](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) to start a new line yourself.
480	- Text is drawn at no more than 8,192 px on a side, so a box stops growing there whatever **Width** says.
481	- With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Mode**, **Width** and the side handles set the action's end, like any other text property.
482	
483	## With an agent
484	
485	`set_text` sets the box through `width`: a wrap width in pixels, or `null` to go back to Auto-size. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
486	
487	## Related
488	
489	- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
490	- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
491	- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
492	- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
493	=== text-reveal
494	---
495	title: "Text reveals"
496	description: "Make a text clip type on, fade in word by word or rise in line by line, and set how long it takes to arrive and leave."
497	---
498	
499	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
500	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
501	
502	A reveal decides how a text clip's words arrive and leave. It runs from the clip's own first and last frames, so it needs no [action](/motion/actions/) and it moves with the clip.
503	
504	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Reveal" tools="set_text" />
505	
506	## Add a reveal
507	
508	<Steps>
509	
510	1. Select the text clip.
511	
512	2. In the inspector's **Clip** tab, open the **Reveal** section of the **Text** sub-tab.
513	
514	3. Choose **Typewriter**, **Word Fade** or **Line Rise** from the **Reveal** popup.
515	
516	4. Set [**In** and **Out**](#set-how-long-it-takes) if you want something other than one second in and no exit.
517	
518	</Steps>
519	
520	Switching from one reveal to another keeps the times you set. Choosing **None**, or the section's **Reset**, turns the reveal off and forgets them, so the next reveal starts at 1 s in and 0 s out.
521	
522	When the section is closed, its header reads "off", or the reveal and its **In** time, such as "typewriter · 1.00 s".
523	
524	The preview, a rendered frame and an export all work out each frame the same way, so what you see while scrubbing is what you'll export.
525	
526	## The three reveals
527	
528	### Typewriter
529	
530	The text types on, one character at a time. Spaces and line breaks count as characters, so the typing pauses at them. On the way out it backspaces, and the end of the text goes first.
531	
532	### Word Fade
533	
534	The words fade in one after another. Each word's fade overlaps the next by half, so it reads as a wave across the text rather than one word at a time. On the way out they leave in the same order, so the first word in is the first word out.
535	
536	### Line Rise
537	
538	Each line fades in as it rises into place, starting 35 % of its own height below where it ends up. The top line goes first and the others follow. On the way out each line sinks and fades, again from the top.
539	
540	A line on its way up is cut off at the edge of the text box. Over a [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) that looks like a mask, and without one the line appears to slide out of nothing.
541	
542	Lines are what the box makes them. In [Auto-size](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) only your own line breaks start a new line, so a single line of text rises all at once.
543	
544	## Set how long it takes
545	
546	| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
547	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
548	| **In** | How long the arrival takes, from the clip's first frame. | 1 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |
549	| **Out** | How long the departure takes, counted back from the clip's last frame. | 0 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |
550	
551	- A time of 0 means that end of the reveal doesn't happen. With **In** at 0 the text is whole on the first frame, and with **Out** at 0 it stays whole to the last.
552	- Both times snap to whole frames.
553	- Both rows are greyed while **Reveal** is **None**.
554	- If **In** and **Out** add up to more than the clip's length, the two overlap. The text never shows in full, and a short clip gets a partial reveal.
555	
556	A reveal has no easing control, because the motion is part of the reveal you choose.
557	
558	## Word styles take over
559	
560	On a caption page with a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), the word style decides how the words appear. The **Reveal** section is greyed and notes "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply." The page is drawn without any reveal.
561	
562	## Good to know
563	
564	- **Backdrop and outline.** A backdrop stays at full strength for the whole clip, so the words type or fade onto it. An outline arrives and leaves with its letters.
565	- **Trimming.** **In** and **Out** are measured from the clip's edges, so a trim moves the reveal with the new edge and keeps its length.
566	- **Splitting.** After a [split](/editing/splitting/), the first piece keeps the arrival and loses the departure, and the second keeps the departure and loses the arrival. A piece left with neither has its reveal turned off.
567	- **Transitions.** A reveal starts on the clip's first frame, so a [transition](/motion/transitions/) into a text clip plays over the start of the reveal.
568	- **Nests.** Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the text clip's own edges count, not the nest clip's. If the nest clip's edge falls part way through a reveal, the reveal is cut off there.
569	- **Actions.** With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, these rows set the action's end. A change of reveal switches at the action's end rather than blending. **In** and **Out** ramp like any number, which shifts the reveal's own timing while it plays, so it's usually better to set them on the clip.
570	- **Right-to-left text.** Typewriter can show the wrong part of a line when the text is right-to-left or mixes directions.
571	
572	## With an agent
573	
574	`set_text` sets a reveal through `animation`: `null` turns it off, and `{kind, in, out}` sets it, with a `kind` of `typewriter`, `word_fade` or `line_rise`. On a page with a `word_style`, the word style is what's drawn and `animation` has no effect. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
575	
576	## Related
577	
578	- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
579	- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
580	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
581	- [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/)
